plan.title: Octopuses Have Three Hearts
plan.description:
Why an octopus needs three hearts.

Sources:
https://ocean.si.edu/

Narration is AI-generated. #Shorts

segments.narration: Octopuses have three hearts, and their blood is blue. That sounds like science fiction, but it is completely real.
Two of those hearts pump blood through the gills, where it picks up oxygen from the water around them.
The third heart then pushes that oxygen rich blood around the rest of the body, to the arms and the brain.
Their blood uses a copper based molecule instead of iron, and copper is what turns it blue instead of red.
Here is the twist. The main heart actually stops beating while the octopus swims, which is why they tire so fast.
So most of the time they would rather crawl along the sea floor than swim. Now you know.
